T: One day in Rome. Gelato on the steps.
D: A runaway princess spends a day in Rome with an American reporter who knows exactly who she is.
P: Serve dessert when Ann sits on the Spanish Steps with her gelato.
S: the princess's day out in Rome
Risotto balls with a mozzarella centre, crumbed and fried at 180C until golden, served with a little tomato sauce.
Whipped ricotta, fig and honey crostini
Ann ordering champagne at the pavement café

Toasted baguette spread with lemony whipped ricotta, topped with fresh fig, a drizzle of honey, crushed pistachios and a few thyme leaves. Slice 1 baguette into 20 thin rounds, brush with olive oil and toast at 200C for 8 minutes. Beat 250g fresh ricotta with the zest of 1 lemon, 2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt until fluffy. Spread on the toasts. Cut 5 fresh figs into quarters and press one onto each. Drizzle with 2 tbsp honey, then scatter 30g crushed pistachios and a few thyme leaves. Serve with a glass of something sparkling.
the wild Vespa ride through Rome
Ciabatta sliced, toasted with olive oil and rubbed with garlic, topped with chopped tomato, basil and salt.
M: Spaghetti tossed with pecorino, cracked black pepper and a splash of the pasta water until creamy.
the dance on the barge by the Tiber

Chicken thighs browned and braised in tomato, red wine, olives, capers and rosemary until falling apart, with crusty bread for the sauce. Season 8 bone-in chicken thighs and brown well in 2 tbsp olive oil for 8 minutes. Remove. Cook 1 sliced onion, 1 sliced red capsicum and 3 garlic cloves for 5 minutes. Add 125ml red wine and reduce by half, then 800g tinned tomatoes, 2 rosemary sprigs, 80g kalamata olives and 1 tbsp capers. Return the chicken, cover and simmer 40 minutes, uncovering for the last 10 to thicken. Scatter with parsley and serve with ciabatta.
W: Ann eating gelato on the Spanish Steps
Vanilla ice cream and lemon sorbet scooped into cones or glasses, finished with crushed amaretti biscuits on top.
K: Hot espresso shaken hard over ice with a little sugar syrup until frothy, strained into chilled martini glasses with a twist of lemon. Chill 4 martini glasses. Pull 4 double shots of espresso, about 240ml. Working in two batches, fill a cocktail shaker with ice, add half the espresso and 20ml sugar syrup, and shake hard for 20 seconds until thick and foamy. Strain into two glasses. Repeat. Twist a strip of lemon peel over each glass and serve immediately while the foam is still standing.

s.note: the princess's day out in Rome
s.how: Cook 300g arborio rice into a risotto with stock and parmesan and chill overnight. Roll into ovals around a cube of mozzarella. Coat in beaten egg and panko and fry at 180C until golden. Serve hot with a little warm napoli sauce.

s.note: the wild Vespa ride through Rome
s.how: Slice a ciabatta, brush with olive oil and toast until golden. Rub each slice with a cut garlic clove. Chop 4 ripe tomatoes with torn basil, olive oil and salt and pile on top. Eat quickly before you zoom off on a scooter.

m.how: Cook 500g spaghetti and keep a cup of the pasta water. Toast a spoon of cracked black pepper in a little butter. Add the pasta and a splash of water, then toss in 150g finely grated pecorino off the heat until creamy. Serve straight away.

w.note: Ann eating gelato on the Spanish Steps
w.how: Scoop vanilla ice cream and lemon sorbet into waffle cones or small glasses. Crush a few amaretti biscuits and scatter over the top. Eat it sitting on the steps, the way a runaway princess would on her one day off.

d.how: Chill 4 martini glasses. Pull 4 double shots of espresso, about 240ml. Working in two batches, fill a cocktail shaker with ice, add half the espresso and 20ml sugar syrup, and shake hard for 20 seconds until thick and foamy. Strain into two glasses. Repeat. Twist a strip of lemon peel over each glass and serve immediately while the foam is still standing.
